name: MotionSites
tagline: AI generator for animated, motion-heavy marketing sites and landing pages.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is the category where the DIY tool and the product do the same job, except the DIY tool is the coding agent you already pay for. If what you want is one animated landing page for one project, an agent will write you a Next.js page with Framer Motion or GSAP scroll animations in a single session, and you own the code. The generator's real value is repeatability and a visual editor for people who will not touch code, which is a different customer than the one reading this page. You lose the curated template taste and the one-click hosted deploy, both of which are a few hours of work or a Vercel button. If you need ten client sites a month with a non-technical editor in the loop, pay for the tool instead.
coreLoopDIY: Generates a local Next.js one-pager driven by a single content spec file, with a small library of scroll-triggered animated sections and a static export you can host anywhere.
requirements: a Vercel, Netlify or Cloudflare Pages account if you want it publicly hosted
your own copy, images and fonts
whatYouLose: A visual editor, so every change is a code edit
Someone else's design taste, which is the part most people are actually buying
Hosted deploys, preview links and a domain flow that just works
A template library to start from instead of a blank page
Built-in image and asset generation for filler content
moatNotes: Motion design is fussy: easing, stagger and reduced-motion handling are where generated sites usually look cheap. That polish is the product, and it is copyable.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because most buyers of an AI site builder are not going to open a terminal, and the ones who will already have an agent. The paid version sells taste plus a deploy button plus the ability to change the headline six months from now without remembering how the repo works. For a solo dev building one site, none of that is worth a subscription. For a marketer shipping landing pages weekly, it obviously is.
notes: An AI website builder is the one SaaS category a coding agent replaces by definition, since the output is just code.
prompt:
Build a local, self-contained animated landing page kit. No accounts, no backend, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS
- Framer Motion for animation
- Static export via `output: 'export'` so the result is a folder of HTML/CSS/JS

Core idea: all copy and structure live in one file, `content/site.ts`, typed with zod. The page renders sections from that array. Editing the site means editing that file, not the components.

Section components to implement, each with scroll-triggered entrance animation using useInView and a shared easing/stagger config in `lib/motion.ts`:
- Hero: big headline with per-word stagger, subhead, two CTA buttons, optional background gradient mesh
- LogoRow: marquee of client logos, pauses on hover
- FeatureGrid: 3 or 6 cards, staggered fade-and-rise
- Showcase: sticky-scroll section where an image pins while text steps through 3 beats
- Stats: numbers that count up once when in view
- Testimonial: single quote, soft parallax
- FAQ: accordion with animated height
- CTA + Footer

Rules:
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: all animations collapse to instant opacity changes
- Every animation uses the shared easing tokens, no one-off magic numbers
- Fully responsive, mobile first, no horizontal overflow
- Lighthouse-friendly: next/image for images, fonts self-hosted via next/font, no layout shift
- Dark mode via a `class` strategy, default dark

Also build a tiny `scripts/new-site.ts` that copies `content/site.example.ts` to `content/site.ts` so I can start a fresh page fast.

Seed it with plausible placeholder copy for a fake SaaS so `npm run dev` shows a finished-looking page immediately. Write a README with the three commands I need: dev, build, and where the exported static files land. No CMS, no auth, no analytics, no AI copy generation in scope.
